analysis.title: What Matters Today: Risk Views, Hiking at a Slower Pace, Downside Growth Risks, CTAs Selling Nasdaq
key_insights: Rich Privo argues front-end rates have stabilized, which is good for risk. Energy is still too high for comfort but is more likely to produce chop than a sustained selloff absent another escalation.
Credit is flagged as the main worry, still flashing yellow to red relative to equities. A calmer credit market could be a meaningful catalyst for a broader rally.

Hyperscaler earnings and the Fed are the main events this week. Four focus areas: capex (flat/up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks and shovels), backlog conversion to revenue, FCF conversion in the out quarters, and financing (equity vs debt).
GS expects the FOMC to skip a hike at its October meeting and deliver a second hike in December.

The tightening in financial conditions since September is only a bit more than usually associated with one hike and much less than the four hikes the market has priced, so the FOMC is unlikely to see it as excessive or a replacement for hikes.

If the FOMC hikes every other meeting in 2027, March would be the next candidate. GS does not expect a March hike because it expects inflation to improve as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressure effects fade.
Growth concerns or employment weakness would likely end the hiking cycle. Some FOMC participants may share GS's view that the economy is not overheated and prefer to limit the size of the cycle.

Fiscal easing and the AI boom impulse have offset the drag from the war in Iran and higher US tariffs. The AI growth impulse was set to peak in late 2026 or early 2027, and AI investment as a share of GDP is expected to slow over the next year.

Long-term rates are up about 100bp on average across developed-market curves since early 2026. If sustained, GS estimates this subtracts a cumulative 0.6% from GDP via housing, consumer durables and business investment.

The AI-driven wealth effect added an estimated 0.4pp (0.25% of GDP) to US consumer spending growth over the past year. It should fade gradually if stocks perform in line with strategists' expectations, and more sharply if AI-related stocks keep declining.

GS's strongest global view is that central banks will deliver fewer hikes than currently priced. Rates strategists cite underweight positioning, diminished technical risks and risk asset pressures as reasons the recent rally might extend.

Equity strategists are wary of momentum factor exposure given narrow breadth, but expect the S&P 500 to resume its climb after the midterm election as earnings grow. Credit strategists stay cautious on IG technology bonds but see scope for a near-term reversal in HY after the recent selloff.
CTAs sold nearly $3bn of NDX futures over the last three sessions, the largest 3-day selling bout since March 2025.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects only a skip in October and a second hike in December, with inflation improving and no March hike, so central banks deliver fewer hikes than the four priced and the rally can extend.
tension_points.bear_case: The market has priced four hikes, and the FOMC could see the tightening in financial conditions as not excessive, so it could keep hiking at an every-other-meeting pace in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation failing to improve as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade could bring a March hike.

tension_points.bull_case: If credit calms down, it could be a meaningful catalyst for a broader rally, and strategists see scope for a near-term HY reversal.
